title: How Much Discretion Do Your Team Members Have to Execute the Strategy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note explores the tension between execution consistency and team member engagement, arguing that overly scripted execution processes produce mechanical, disengaged compliance, while too little structure produces inconsistent results. The recommended balance is establishing clear standards and guardrails while leaving room for improvisation within those bounds, giving team members enough discretion to adapt to specific situations without losing overall consistency. The piece frames finding this balance as a defining skill of high-performance leadership.
points: Highly scripted execution processes are said to produce consistent but mechanical, disengaged team performance.
Too little structure, conversely, undermines the consistency organizations need from strategy execution.
The recommended approach sets clear quality standards and guardrails while allowing improvisation within them.
Team members given appropriate discretion are said to execute with more ownership, passion, and enthusiasm.
Finding the right balance between constraint and flexibility is framed as where effective leadership lives.
quotes: Unfortunately, executing strategy with key processes, tasks, and actions that are highly scripted produces team member engagement that is both mechanical and superficial.
Too much execution rigor without flexibility and team members disengage. Too little constraint or scripting and team members operate without the stability to create replicable results.
They spend the time to articulate what great execution looks like and to make sure everyone understands the guardrails that keep everyone in the same lane.
When team members enjoy the autonomy to improvise how they enact the strategy within a set of guidelines, they execute with passion and enthusiasm and take ownership for outcomes.
Great execution across the enterprise requires finding the right balance between constraint and flexibility.
